transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Cleveland, Ohio, I'm Dale Willman.
With two days left before the midterm elections,
President Trump was campaigning in Kansas Sunday,
urging Republicans to show up at the polls.
Republicans, we love them.
They're keeping our country.
Well, actually, they're making it because we had four years,
which were a disaster.
And we've just made it.
In two years, what we've done is unprecedented.
America is great again.
America is great again.
Concerns, meanwhile, continue over the integrity of balloting.
The Trump administration has initiated an increasing number of lawsuits
in Alaska and elsewhere.
They include efforts to restrict some mail-in ballots
and their challenging voter registration roles in California and elsewhere.
Democratic Congressman Jamie Raskin says there's an easy fix.
If the federal government stays out of it and lets the state government
authorities actually run the elections the way that we always have,
we will have free and fair elections.
The problem is, as this judge found in a very important ruling,
that the Trump administration keeps trying to stick its nose
into state electoral administration when it has no constitutional role there.
Raskin was speaking Sunday on NBC's "Meet the Press" show.
A private jet on its way to the Bahamas from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport
crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida on Sunday.
All nine passengers on board were killed.
Katie McAfee from member station KUT has more.
Early reports suggest severe weather caused the plane to go from controlled flight
to a near vertical nosedive to the ground within minutes.
The plane was descending over 20,000 feet per minute before impact.
Aviation attorney Mike Slack said the weather conditions in Florida
would not have been suitable for any aircraft.
The most significant question this whole accident that I see
is how and why the airplane ended up where it did
in dangerous proximity to the weather.
At a news conference, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said
there were no reports of injuries to people on the ground.
The investigation into the crash is ongoing.
For NPR News, I'm Katie McAfee in Austin.
Four people were killed and at least 15 others injured
following several shootings in Dallas's Deep Elm neighborhood early Sunday morning.
Penelope Rivera with member station KERA reports.
Dallas Police Chief Daniel Como told reporters
three separate shootings occurred within minutes of each other.
It's not clear if the shootings were related
and police did not identify the people who died.
Authorities say the total number of people injured
is still being determined, as some people took themselves to the hospital.
Police arrested one suspect and were still looking for others Sunday.
This is at least the third fatal incident in the Deep Elm neighborhood this year,
raising concerns over public safety in the area.
For NPR News, I'm Penelope Rivera in Dallas.
There were several other shootings elsewhere in the country,
including one in Alabama that left one person dead and eight others injured.
You're listening to NPR News.
Tens of thousands of people protested in New Delhi, India, Sunday
against the government of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
They were calling for the resignation of the country's election chief
because of a contentious revision to voter rolls.
The revision has removed more than 130 million names
from voter rolls since last year.
The U.S. Capitol Christmas tree that was harvested in north Idaho last month
is now on tour as it makes its way to Washington, D.C.
From member station Boise State Public Radio,
Lauren Patterson went to one of the first whistle stops in Orofino on Sunday.
The 76-foot-tall U.S. Capitol Christmas tree has been encased
in the back of a big semi-truck.
But the top is made of wooden beams and glass
so people can see the colorful lights and handmade ornaments
covering the green spruce branches.
The whistle stop tour turned the local grocery store parking lot
into a hub of activity with people of all ages.
Many of the locals have come out to see and take pictures with the tree.
Christy Skinner is one of them.
When we get to turn the TV on on Christmas and New Year's and watch it,
they'd be just really proud to know that it came from here.
The tree has more scheduled whistle stops throughout Idaho,
Montana, Wyoming, and the Midwest before arriving at its final destination.
For NPR News, I'm Lauren Patterson in Orofino, Idaho.
Kimi Antonelli has become the youngest champion
in the history of Formula One racing, the 20-year-old drives for Mercedes.
He took the lead for the championship following Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix.
Antonelli is also the first Italian to win the title
since Alberto Escari in 1953.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: President Trump campaigns in Kansas, urging Republicans to vote before midterm elections
Trump administration lawsuits over mail-in ballots and voter rolls draw concern about election integrity
Rep. Jamie Raskin says federal government should stay out of state election administration
Private jet bound for Bahamas crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine aboard
Deep Elm neighborhood shootings in Dallas leave four dead and at least 15 injured
Shooting in Alabama leaves one dead and eight injured
Tens of thousands protest in New Delhi against Modi government over voter roll revision
U.S. Capitol Christmas tree from north Idaho begins whistle stop tour toward Washington, D.C.
Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest Formula One champion after Mexico City Grand Prix
